title: "GDP vs NEET Analysis"
author: "Vasiliki"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: pdf_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

ALPHA <- 0.05
```

# Import Data
```{r import_data}
gdp_df <- read_csv("/Users/vasilikimichalia/Desktop/IDS_Group_Proj-main/Exported_data/gdp_per_capita_df.csv")
neet_df <- read_csv("/Users/vasilikimichalia/Desktop/IDS_Group_Proj-main/Exported_data/youth_not_in_eet.csv")
```

# Merge & Clean
```{r merge_clean}
# Perform an inner join to combine GDP and NEET datasets
# Matching rows where Entity (country name), Code (country code), and Year all align
merged_df <- inner_join(gdp_df, neet_df, by = c("Entity", "Code", "Year"))

# Clean and restructure the merged dataset
merged_df <- merged_df %>%
  # Rename columns for clarity (Entity -> Country, keep only one Continent column)
  rename(
    Country   = Entity,
    Continent = Continent.x
  ) %>%
  # Select only the columns needed for analysis
  select(Continent, Country, Year, Gdp_per_capita, Perc_youth_not_in_eet) %>%
  # Convert GDP and NEET columns to numeric type to ensure proper calculations
  mutate(
    Gdp_per_capita        = as.numeric(Gdp_per_capita),
    Perc_youth_not_in_eet = as.numeric(Perc_youth_not_in_eet)
  ) %>%
  # Remove any rows with missing values to ensure complete cases for analysis
  na.omit()

# Convert Continent to a factor (categorical variable) for grouping and visualization
merged_df$Continent <- as.factor(merged_df$Continent)
```

# Global Correlation
```{r global_correlation}
# Perform a Pearson correlation test at the global (country) level
# Tests the linear relationship between GDP per capita and NEET percentage
# across all countries and years in the dataset
global_cor <- cor.test(
  merged_df$Gdp_per_capita,
  merged_df$Perc_youth_not_in_eet,
  method = "pearson"
)

# Display correlation results (r value, p-value, confidence interval)
global_cor
```

# Global Plot
```{r global_plot}
# Create a scatter plot showing the relationship between GDP and NEET at country level
g1 <- ggplot(merged_df, aes(Gdp_per_capita, Perc_youth_not_in_eet, color = Continent)) +
  # Add semi-transparent points, colored by continent
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  # Add a black linear regression line (without confidence interval shading)
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black") +
  # Use log scale on x-axis to better visualize the wide range of GDP values
  scale_x_log10() +
  # Add informative labels
  labs(
    title = "GDP per Capita vs NEET (%) — Global",
    x = "GDP per Capita (log scale)",
    y = "NEET (%)"
  ) +
  # Apply a clean, minimal theme
  theme_minimal()

# Display the plot
g1
```

# Continent Means + Correlation
```{r continent_means}
# Aggregate data to the continent level by calculating mean values
continent_means <- merged_df %>%
  # Group all observations by continent
  group_by(Continent) %>%
  # Calculate the mean GDP and mean NEET percentage for each continent
  summarise(
    Mean_GDP  = mean(Gdp_per_capita),
    Mean_NEET = mean(Perc_youth_not_in_eet),
    .groups   = "drop"  # Remove grouping structure after summarizing
  )

# Perform correlation test on continent-level aggregated data
# This tests whether continents with higher average GDP have lower average NEET
continent_cor <- cor.test(
  continent_means$Mean_GDP,
  continent_means$Mean_NEET,
  method = "pearson"
)

# Display correlation results for continent-level analysis
continent_cor
```

# Continent Plot
```{r continent_plot}
# Create a scatter plot of the 6 continent means
g2 <- ggplot(continent_means, aes(Mean_GDP, Mean_NEET)) +
  # Add larger points for each continent, colored by continent
  geom_point(size = 4, aes(color = Continent)) +
  # Label each point with the continent name, positioned above the point
  geom_text(aes(label = Continent), vjust = -1) +
  # Add a black linear regression line showing the continent-level trend
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "black") +
  # Use log scale on x-axis for consistency with global plot
  scale_x_log10() +
  # Add informative labels
  labs(
    title = "Mean GDP vs Mean NEET — Continent Level",
    x = "Mean GDP per Capita (log scale)",
    y = "Mean NEET (%)"
  ) +
  # Apply clean, minimal theme
  theme_minimal()

# Display the continent-level plot
g2
```
```{r results_table}
# Create a summary table comparing the two levels of analysis
# Build a clean hypothesis test results table
results_table <- data.frame(
  # Label each analysis level
  Level = c("Global (Countries)", "Continent Means (6 points)"),
  # Extract Pearson correlation coefficients from both tests
  Pearson_r = c(global_cor$estimate, continent_cor$estimate),
  # Extract p-values to assess statistical significance
  p_value = c(global_cor$p.value, continent_cor$p.value),
  # Record sample sizes (number of observations in each analysis)
  N = c(nrow(merged_df), nrow(continent_means)),
  # Determine if results are statistically significant at the alpha level
  Significant = c(global_cor$p.value < ALPHA,
                  continent_cor$p.value < ALPHA)
)

# Display the results table for easy comparison
results_table
```
